paper_title: Efficient and Stable Quasiplanar Heterojunction Solar Cells with an AcetoxySubstituted Wide-Bandgap Polymer

knowledge_points.content: Two new wide-bandgap copolymers, PNTB-OAc and PNTB-OH, were synthesized by incorporating acetoxy and hydroxy groups, respectively, onto the termini of alkyl chains of electron-deficient units.
knowledge_points.evidence: Herein, we report two new copolymers for Q-PHJ solar cells synthesized by the addition of hydroxy (PNTB-OH) and acetoxy groups (PNTB-OAc) onto electron-deficient units.

knowledge_points.content: The PNTB-OAc:N3-based quasiplanar heterojunction (Q-PHJ) solar cell achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 16.53%, which is approximately 2.4 times higher than the 6.79% PCE achieved by the PNTB-OH:N3 device.
knowledge_points.evidence: PNTB-OAc-based Q-PHJ OSCs realized the highest photovoltaic performance of 16.53%, which is ~2.4 times higher than 6.79% obtained from the PNTB-OH-based Q-PHJ OSCs.

knowledge_points.content: Single-crystal analysis reveals that the acetoxy-substituted unit (NTI-OAc) forms regular hydrogen bonds with adjacent molecules, leading to a shorter π-π stacking distance and more ordered molecular packing compared to the hydroxy-substituted unit.
knowledge_points.evidence: The single-crystal data reveals more regular stacking and order orientation driven by hydrogen bonding, of the acetoxy-substituted electron-deficient units... NTI-OAc possesses a shorter π··π stacking distance and ordered molecular packing in the solid state.

knowledge_points.content: PNTB-OAc:N3 devices exhibit higher and more balanced charge transport, with hole and electron mobilities of 4.2 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 and 3.2 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1, respectively.
knowledge_points.evidence: the measured hole mobilities of the PNTB-OAc:N3... are 4.2 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1... The electron mobilities for PNTB-OAc:N3-based Q-PHJ devices are 3.2 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1... Higher hole/ electron mobility and also more balanced charge transport were exhibited by PNTB-OAc:N3-based Q-PHJ devices.

knowledge_points.content: The PNTB-OAc-based device demonstrates lower nonradiative energy loss (ΔE3 = 0.213 eV) compared to the PNTB-OH-based device (ΔE3 = 0.231 eV), contributing to a higher open-circuit voltage.
knowledge_points.evidence: The ΔE3 values of PNTB-OAc:N3- and PNTB-OH:N3-based Q-PHJ devices are 0.213 and 0.231, respectively. Hence, the presence of the acetoxy functional group reduces the overall energy losses, which are attributed to low nonradiative energy losses (ΔE3).

knowledge_points.content: GIWAXS analysis shows that PNTB-OAc has a longer crystal coherence length (CCL) of 35.30 Å in the (100) direction and 9.81 Å in the (010) direction, indicating higher crystallinity than PNTB-OH.
knowledge_points.evidence: The crystal coherence length (CCL) of PNTB-OAc and PNTB-OH neat film in the (100) direction are 35.30 and 29.82 Å, respectively. In the (010) direction, the crystal coherence length (CCL) of PNTB-OAc is 9.81 Å, which is much longer than that observed for PNTB-OH (8.69 Å).

knowledge_points.content: PNTB-OAc:N3 Q-PHJ devices exhibit excellent photostability, retaining over 85% of their initial PCE after 1050 hours of continuous illumination under nitrogen.
knowledge_points.evidence: PNTB-OAc device demonstrated superior photostability and storage stability, retained more than 85% of the initial PCE after illumination for 1050h.

knowledge_points.content: The storage stability of PNTB-OAc:N3 devices is robust, with 90% of the initial PCE retained after 1600 hours of storage in a nitrogen atmosphere.
knowledge_points.evidence: PNTB-OAc device... retained... 90% of the initial PCE under nitrogen for 1600h.

knowledge_points.content: The Q-PHJ active layers were fabricated using sequential solution processing with orthogonal solvents, where the polymer donor was dissolved in chlorobenzene and the N3 acceptor in chloroform.
knowledge_points.evidence: In quasiplanar heterojunction (Q-PHJ) solar cells, the active layers were prepared by sequential processing with orthogonal solvents... using a solution of polymers in chlorobenzene and a solution of N3 in chloroform.

knowledge_points.content: Dynamic X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (DXPS) confirmed the vertical distribution of the Q-PHJ films, showing an enrichment of the N3 acceptor (identified by fluorine signals) in the upper layer of the film.
knowledge_points.evidence: In both the polymers Q-PHJ as the etching depth increases, the F 1s signals gradually weaken until they disappear... indicating the enrichment of N3 in the upper layer of the Q-PHJ films.

knowledge_points.content: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) reveals that the PNTB-OAc:N3 film has a much smoother surface (Rq = 0.56 nm) compared to the PNTB-OH:N3 film (Rq = 2.3 nm), facilitating better interface contact.
knowledge_points.evidence: the PNTB-OAc:N3 Q-PHJ film exhibits a root-mean-square surface roughness (Rq) value of 0.56 nm while that for PNTB-OH:N3 Q-PHJ film is 2.3 nm.

knowledge_points.content: PNTB-OAc and PNTB-OH polymers exhibit high thermal stability with 5% weight loss temperatures of 409 °C and 345 °C, respectively, as determined by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA).
knowledge_points.evidence: 5% weight loss was recorded for PNTB-OAc at 409 °C, and by PNTB-OH at 345 °C. Both polymers have enough thermal stability to tolerate device fabrication.
